subject: [PATCH 1/5] mm: limit pagecache folio refcount when mapping pages

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer questioned whether the slow path needs to be inlined at all call sites, suggesting that only the likely() check should remain inlined and the rest moved to a function call

Reviewer David (Arm) suggested using capable_noaudit() instead of capable(), as cap_vm_enough_memory() already checks admin reserve with CAP_OPT_NOAUDIT, and a refused reference should not leave an audit record.
reviews.raw_body:
It's not a lot of code. Do we really care?

E.g., in gup.c, the compiler is free to not inline into each of the two callsites.

---

Not an expert, but capable_noaudit() sounds good.

Not sure if that fully resolves sashiko's complaint in the last commit.

Thanks!

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-11-06.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code that limits pagecache folio refcounts when mapping pages, moving the unlikely path into a separate function to reduce inline code duplication and improve maintainability.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David expressed concern about the exported symbol requirement for fuse, which is now necessary due to the patch's refactoring

Reviewer David (Arm) suggested replacing capable() with has_capability_noaudit() for checking admin reserves, citing cap_vm_enough_memory()'s use of CAP_OPT_NOAUDIT and expressing hope that this is the correct approach.
reviews.raw_body:
Okay, I ended up splitting it up. A bit nsaty now that fuse will require an
exported symbol.

---

Ok, the noaudit definitely seems to be the right thing. But getting overlayfs +
fuse oddities done "better", I am using has_capability_noaudit(current,
CAP_SYS_RESOURCE) now.

Hoping that is the right thing to use now ... review appreciated.

-- 
Cheers,

David
